anomaly_def.Name: Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly + Transaction Log Subsystem Anomaly + Storage Space Capacity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Composite Definition: The database is simultaneously suffering from (1) severe buffer-cache page and latch contention, (2) a saturated or stalled transaction-log subsystem, and (3) imminent or actual exhaustion of physical or logical storage space. These three root causes coexist and interact, creating a self-reinforcing bottleneck that impairs both read and write paths, inflates CPU usage, and threatens service availability.

Combined Observable Phenomena: Users experience sharp spikes in response time for both read and commit operations. Wait-event statistics show surging buffer-busy, page-latch, log-flush, log-sync, checkpoint, and space-allocation waits. Checkpoints and log switches fire more frequently yet take longer to finish; archive or replica-shipping lag grows. Free-space alarms oscillate near 0 %, autoextend and archive writes fail, and "cannot allocate extent" or "out of space" errors appear. Dirty buffers pile up because they cannot be flushed promptly—first due to log flush delays, then because datafiles or log destinations have no room—causing hot pages to remain latched and provoke CPU spin as sessions queue. Overall throughput collapses while CPU, log-file I/O, and storage error counters soar.

Causal Interaction: Slow or blocked log flushing elongates commit latency and stretches checkpoint intervals, keeping many buffers dirty and pinned. These long-lived pins elevate latch contention on hot pages, amplifying the buffer-cache anomaly. Simultaneously, dwindling storage space prevents timely auto-extension of datafiles and the creation or archival of new log segments, further stalling log writes. Each stalled log write prolongs dirty-page residency, which in turn increases buffer turnover pressure and latch competition. The clogged log and space exhaustion thus feed buffer contention, while the intensified write bursts generated by retried transactions and checkpoint storms accelerate space consumption, pushing the system into a cascading failure loop.

entry.official_definition: Controls how long STOP REPLICA waits before timing out.
entry.trigger_condition: A STOP REPLICA administrative operation waits longer than rpl_stop_replica_timeout.
entry.workload_impact: The administrative replication stop operation times out.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL replication system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when replication endpoints stop exchanging or applying data within the configured timeout window, causing the channel to be considered inactive.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect replication channel health, sender/receiver status, upstream and downstream connectivity, and whether lag or stalled apply is preventing timely progress.
